changes.finding: BC Builds: passes the published items this screen checks: non-residential space is 15.7% of area, under the 30% cap; ground must break within 12 to 18 months of the conditional land contribution letter. BC Builds works opportunity by opportunity; middle-income rents and the team's capacity are not assessed here.

5 storeys puts the building under Part 3 of the BC Building Code 2024 and the Vancouver Building By-law 2025; wood frame is standard to 6 storeys and encapsulated mass timber is permitted to 18 under the VBBL; seismic changes apply to permits from 2026-09-15.

Community Housing Fund: passes the eligibility items this screen checks: unit mix matches 30/50/20 within tolerance; site control (council resolution) meets the readiness bar; construction must be able to start within 18 months of award. Not assessed here: need and demand, the operator's capacity, the fund's rated criteria and the budget. Its 2025 call did not proceed (February 2026), so no intake is open now; the program page says it will post when next seeking proposals (as of 22 Sep 2026).

Would be a program for this housing if it is Indigenous-led, or partnered with an Indigenous housing provider or Nation (not said on the option): affordable rental homes for Indigenous families, Elders, individuals and people with disabilities, on and off reserve; every home rent geared to income (fixed rents may be considered on reserve). It funds building the homes (the Province's funding programs page: "funding to build and to support the creation of" them). A project enters by BC Housing's request for proposals. No intake is open now (closed: no call is posted on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026)). Its homes are all rent geared to income; this option has 26 market-rent homes, which it would not carry. Its criteria are not tested here.
32 of 88 units (36.4%) have two or more bedrooms, against a 35.0% minimum.
Eligible for consideration as 100% social housing under the policy, within the staff benchmark.
No minimum off-street parking applies citywide since June 2024; the option provides 40 vehicle and 220 bicycle spaces. Bicycle spaces are set by the Parking By-law at the development permit stage.
FSR 2.49 exceeds the outright maximum of 1.2, so it is not allowed outright; rezoning is required (CD-1 under the Interim Rezoning Policy for Social Housing), where density is negotiated.
Height 18.3 m exceeds the outright maximum of 10.7 m, so it is not allowed outright; rezoning is required (CD-1 under the Interim Rezoning Policy for Social Housing), where height is negotiated.
Schedule C requires 20 trees on 2,811 m²; the option keeps 1 of 9 and plants 19, leaving 20, which meets the minimum.
